figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. 1 (left) and 2 (right) suppressed the RANKL-induced MAPK signaling. RAW264.7 cells were treated with 1 and 2 in the presence or
absence of 100 ng/mL RANKL for 60 min. Phosphorylated and total ERK1/2-JNK1/2-p38 MAPKs were determined by Western blot. GAPDH
was used as the loading control. Quantitative analyses of p-ERK1/2, p-JNK1/2, or p-P38 MAPK expression relative to ERK1/2, JNK1/2, or P38
MAPKs, respectively, by densitometry were conducted. Data represent the mean ± SD with three independent experiments (*p < 0.05 vs the
blank; #p < 0.05 vs the RANKL-induced control group). 1 and 2 suppressed the RANKL-induced NF-κB signaling by inhibiting NF-κB nuclear
translocation. RAW264.7 cells were treated with 1 and 2 in the presence or absence of 100 ng/mL RANKL for 60 min. P65 levels in the nucleus
and cytoplasm were measured by Western blot. Quantitative analyses of Nuclear p-P65 relative to cytoplasmic p65 by densitometry were
conducted.
